AI ANALYSIS

Data-Driven Betting Insights

Scottie Scheffler towers over the PGA Championship field with a +2.87 SG Total (best in the field by 0.64 strokes) and our model projects a 13.8% win probability — more than double the implied odds at +624. Bryson DeChambeau presents perhaps the most compelling narrative value play: his SG Total of +1.40 ranks only 14th in the field, yet his extraordinary course history (T2 in 2025, 2nd in 2024, T4 in 2023) and +0.109 course fit adjustment make him dangerously underpriced at +3241. Cameron Young quietly profiles as a top-tier contender at +1607 with the third-best SG Total in the field (+2.13) and a strong +0.118 course fit, yet he draws a fraction of the attention of players ranked below him in our model.
Scheffler Is the Clear Alpha Play
Scottie Scheffler leads the field in SG Total (+2.87), SG Approach (#1 at +1.08), and SG Putting (#2 at +0.55) — a rare combination of elite ball-striking and putting. His model win probability of 13.8% at +624 makes him the strongest edge in the field, and his PGA Championship history (1st, T8, T2 over the last three years) is immaculate.
Scottie Scheffler
DeChambeau's History Screams Live Longshot
At +3241, Bryson DeChambeau carries the best three-year PGA Championship history in the field (T2-2nd-T4) and a +0.109 course fit adjustment that ranks among the highest. His 3.0% model win probability against an implied 0.03% at the current price represents roughly 100x value on paper — the kind of asymmetric bet you build a card around.
Bryson DeChambeau
Cameron Young: Stealth Top-3 Profile
Cameron Young's +2.13 SG Total ranks third in the entire 156-player field, yet his +1607 price implies far less respect than Jon Rahm (+1576) who sits just one spot above him in the model. Young's +0.118 course fit is the second-highest among the top 10, and our model gives him a 5.9% win probability — nearly identical to Rahm's 6.0%.
Cameron Young Jon Rahm
Rory's Course Fit Leads the Favorites
Rory McIlroy boasts the highest course fit adjustment among any player in the top 10 at +0.158, significantly above Scheffler (+0.098) and Schauffele (+0.096). At +1224 with a 7.5% model win probability and the fourth-best SG Total (+2.11), McIlroy is the top course-specific overlay among chalk plays despite a soft T47 finish in 2025.
Rory McIlroy
Aberg's Missed Cuts Are a Red Flag
Ludvig Aberg carries an elite +1.90 SG Total (fifth in the field), but his PGA Championship history is alarming: missed cuts in both 2024 and 2025. At +2311 with a 4.2% model probability, the raw talent is undeniable, but bettors should tread carefully when a player hasn't proven he can survive the weekend at this major.
Ludvig Aberg
Fitzpatrick Surging Into Major Form
Matt Fitzpatrick posted a T8 at the 2025 PGA Championship and carries a +1.80 SG Total (seventh in the field) at +3135 odds. Our model assigns him a 3.1% win probability, and his methodical game — built on precision iron play — should thrive this week, though his +0.042 course fit is modest compared to other contenders.
Matt Fitzpatrick
Cantlay Headlines a Loaded Longshot Tier
Patrick Cantlay at +5425 leads our longshot group with an 18.2% top-10 probability and a +1.51 SG Total. His PGA Championship track record includes a T9 in 2023, and at this price, a top-5 or top-10 wager offers significant expected value for a player with clear top-tier skill metrics.
Patrick Cantlay
Morikawa's Irons Make Him Dangerous
Collin Morikawa ranks third in the field in SG Approach at +0.90 — trailing only Scheffler and Rahm — yet sits at +7563 odds. As a former PGA Championship winner who thrives when iron play is at a premium, Morikawa at this price is a high-upside tournament wager worth a small-unit sprinkle.
Collin Morikawa
Schauffele's Defending Title at Fair Price
Xander Schauffele won the 2024 PGA Championship and carries a solid +1.86 SG Total with elite ball-striking (SG Approach +0.86, 4th in field). At +1845 with a 5.1% model win probability, the defending champion is fairly priced — not a screaming value, but a reliable anchor for any outright portfolio.
Xander Schauffele
Min Woo Lee: Best Risk-Reward Longshot
Min Woo Lee at +5471 offers a 17.2% top-10 probability and a +1.50 SG Total that ranks just behind Patrick Cantlay among longshots. His well-rounded game and aggressive style make him a prime candidate for each-way or top-10 placement bets in a field where bombs-and-wedges players can separate from the pack.
Min Woo Lee
